item.title: Did early humans collect keepsakes 500,000 years ago?
item.description: Most of us are familiar with the urge to pick up a seashell from the beach or keep a stone from a hiking trip. The object itself may be ordinary, but to the person who keeps it, it serves as a reminder of a particular moment, place or person. Where did this behavior come from? Did early humans do the same? A new study by Tel Aviv University researchers suggests that this practice stretches back approximately half a million years, with important consequences for the evolution of memory. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: US Defense Secretary Hegseth faces expected impeachment vote this week
item.description: A Republican lawmaker moved Monday to impeach US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the war in Iran, setting up a potentially explosive vote in Congress days after President Donald Trump's party suffered a crushing midterm defeat. Kentucky congressman Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment accusing Hegseth of illegally waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from Washington. Publicado también por: The Hindu - International. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Árabes, ultraortodoxos o Netanyahu: los escenarios de Eisenkot para formar gobierno en Israel
item.description: Terminaron las consultas y este lunes 9 de noviembre arrancó el plazo de 28 días que tiene Gadi Eisenkot para intentar formar un gobierno en Israel. Hay varios escenarios: aliarse con los árabes, con los partidos ultraortodoxos o juntarse con Netanyahu. Cualquier opción trae grandes dificultades que hace, por ahora, casi imposible conseguir los 61 votos necesarios. Si no logra, Netanyahu podría tener la oportunidad de conformar su coalición y continuar en el poder. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
